mainTopic: The rest of the משנה on public fasts for rain (the כהנים on duty, מגילת תענית days, scheduling the fasts), and the גמרא on the ark-and-ashes ritual
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story from the days of רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניא בן תרדיון. The people did not answer אמן after the fast-day ברכות. Instead, the כהנים blew שופר and the leader said 'מי שענה' prayers. The חכמים said this ceremony belonged only at the הר הבית. The משנה then rules on how much the כהנים of the משמר and the בית אב fasted, drank wine, cut their hair and did laundry. It also covers the days next to the holidays in מגילת תענית, which weekday a series of fasts may start on, and fasts that fall on ראש חודש, חנוכה or פורים. The גמרא begins by showing, through רב פפא, that the תיבה-and-ashes ritual is only for the last seven fasts. It explains that the leaders receive ashes first because it is an honor for them. It then asks why someone else puts the ashes on the leaders' heads. רבי אבא דמן קסרי begins his answer, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A prayer leader finishes the blessing and no one answers amen
steps.stepSummary: The story describes a שליח ציבור in the days of רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניא בן תרדיון who finished a fast-day ברכה, but the congregation did not answer אמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the days of רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניא בן תרדיון, someone led the prayers and finished the whole blessing, and the people did not answer amen after him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues a story that began just before this, setting the scene. Someone led the fast-day prayers and nobody said אמן after his ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a congregation answers אמן after a ברכה, so leaving it out is unusual. The story goes on to the attendant's calls for שופר blasts between the ברכות, and then to the חכמים's response to the missing אמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'passed before the ark': led the congregation in prayer
The ark, where the Torah scrolls are kept
The response that confirms a ברכה

steps.confusionAlert: Not answering אמן here is not disrespect. It was the practice in the בית המקדש, and the חכמים will say it belongs there alone. The שופר blasts in the next step are part of the fast-day prayers, not a replacement for the אמן.

phrases.aramaic: בִּימֵי רַבִּי חֲלַפְתָּא וְרַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן תְּרַדְיוֹן
phrases.english: In the days of Rabbi Chalafta and Rabbi Chananya ben Teradyon
that someone passed before the ark
phrases.notes: This means he led the prayers.

phrases.english: and finished the entire blessing,
and they did not answer amen after him.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּימֵי רַבִּי חֲלַפְתָּא וְרַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן תְּרַדְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a story already begun in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In that era, the congregation did not answer אמן after the fast-day ברכה.

steps.title: Calls for shofar blasts between the blessings
steps.stepSummary: After the ברכה, the attendant called for the כהנים to blow a תקיעה, and the ברכה 'מי שענה את אברהם בהר המוריה' followed. Then came a call for a תרועה and the ברכה 'מי שענה את אבותינו על ים סוף'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Blow a תקיעה, כהנים, blow!' 'He Who answered אברהם אבינו on הר המוריה will answer you and hear your cry today.' 'Blow a תרועה, sons of אהרן, blow!' 'He Who answered our fathers at ים סוף will answer you and hear your cry today.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes what came between the ברכות. The attendant called out for the כהנים to blow שופר, and each blast was followed by a 'מי שענה' prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern switches back and forth: first a תקיעה with אברהם at הר המוריה, then a תרועה with our fathers at ים סוף. Each closing asks ה׳ to answer us today the way He answered them in the past.

keyTerms.meaning: Blow a תקיעה, a long, straight blast
Blow a תרועה, a broken, wavering blast
'He Who answered': the opening words of the fast-day prayers

phrases.english: Sound a long blast, priests, sound!
phrases.notes: The synagogue attendant is the one calling this out.

phrases.english: He Who answered Abraham our father
on Mount Moriah,
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry on this day.
Blast a wavering sound, sons of Aaron, blast!

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁעָנָה אֶת אֲבוֹתֵינוּ עַל יַם סוּף,
phrases.english: He Who answered our fathers at the Red Sea,
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry on this day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of step 1 with the שופר blasts between the ברכות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Between the fast-day ברכות, the כהנים blew תקיעות and תרועות, each followed by a 'מי שענה' prayer.

steps.title: The Sages limit leaving out אמן to the Temple
steps.stepSummary: When the חכמים heard about this practice, they said that not answering אמן was done only at the שער מזרח and on the הר הבית, and not elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the matter came before the Sages, they said: We only practiced this way at the Eastern Gate and on the Temple Mount.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים respond to the story. They say that leaving out אמן belongs only in the בית המקדש, not in an ordinary place of prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not reject the ceremony itself. What they limit to the הר הבית is not answering אמן; elsewhere the people answer אמן. Blowing שופר on a fast is done outside the בית המקדש too.

keyTerms.meaning: The Eastern Gate of the Temple Mount

steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, leaving out אמן after the fast-day ברכות was meant only for the בית המקדש. The שופר blasts were not limited to it.

phrases.english: And when the matter came before the Sages,
they said: We did not practice this way,
except at the Eastern Gate and on the Temple Mount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the practice of step 1, not answering אמן
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects leaving out אמן outside the בית המקדש
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not answering אמן was only ever done at the שער מזרח and on the הר הבית

steps.title: רבי יהושע: how much the priests on duty fasted
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהושע, the אנשי משמר and אנשי בית אב fast more as the series of fasts goes on. On the first three, the משמר fasts partly and the בית אב not at all. On the second three, the משמר fasts fully and the בית אב partly. On the final seven, both fast fully.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first three fasts, the men of the watch fast but do not finish, and the men of the family do not fast at all. On the second three, the watch fasts fully, and the family fasts but does not finish. On the last seven, both fast fully. These are the words of רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts a new topic: how the כהנים serving in the בית המקדש take part in the public fasts for rain. רבי יהושע gives a step-by-step scale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בית אב is the family serving on that exact day, so it is always more protected from fasting than the משמר serving that week. This is so they can still do the עבודה. As the fasts become more serious, both groups fast more.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהנים of the watch serving in the בית המקדש that week
The family group within the משמר serving on that particular day
They complete the fast until nightfall

steps.confusionAlert: 'Fast but do not complete' means they start the fast and eat before nightfall. It does not mean skipping the fast entirely.

phrases.english: On the first three fasts —
phrases.notes: These are the public fasts declared when rain does not come.

phrases.english: the men of the watch fast but do not complete,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַנְשֵׁי בֵּית אָב לֹא הָיוּ מִתְעַנִּין כְּלָל.
phrases.english: and the men of the family group did not fast at all.
On the second three —
the men of the watch fast and complete,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַנְשֵׁי בֵּית אָב מִתְעַנִּין וְלֹא מַשְׁלִימִין.
phrases.english: and the men of the family group fast but do not complete.
On the last seven —
both these and those fast and complete,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁלֹשׁ תַּעֲנִיּוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר מִתְעַנִּין וְלֹא מַשְׁלִימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע: on the first three fasts, the משמר fasts partly and the בית אב not at all. On the second three, the משמר fasts fully and the בית אב partly. On the last seven, both fast fully.

steps.title: The Sages: a more lenient scale for the priests
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים move every stage one level more lenient. On the first three fasts, neither group fasts. On the second three, the משמר fasts partly and the בית אב not at all. On the final seven, the משמר fasts fully and the בית אב partly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages say: On the first three fasts, neither group fasts at all. On the second three, the watch fasts but does not finish, and the family does not fast at all. On the last seven, the watch fasts fully, and the family fasts but does not finish.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים disagree with רבי יהושע. They give their own scale, which is easier on the כהנים serving in the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each stage of the חכמים matches the stage before it in רבי יהושע's scale. So the בית אב serving that day never completes a fast, even on the final seven. The disagreement is only about how strict to be. Both agree the scale gets stricter over time.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the Sages say': introduces the opposing view

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע: on the last seven fasts both groups fast fully. חכמים: one stage more lenient throughout, so the בית אב never completes a fast.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
On the first three fasts —

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ לֹא הָיוּ מִתְעַנִּין כְּלָל.
phrases.english: both these and those did not fast at all.
On the second three —
the men of the watch fast but do not complete,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַנְשֵׁי בֵּית אָב לֹא הָיוּ מִתְעַנִּין כְּלָל,
phrases.english: and the men of the family group did not fast at all,
On the last seven —
the men of the watch fast and complete,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַנְשֵׁי בֵּית אָב מִתְעַנִּין וְלֹא מַשְׁלִימִין.
phrases.english: and the men of the family group fast but do not complete.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהושע in step 4 and gives a more lenient scale
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: on the first three fasts, neither group fasts. On the second three, the משמר fasts partly and the בית אב not at all. On the last seven, the משמר fasts fully and the בית אב partly.

steps.title: When the priestly groups may drink wine
steps.stepSummary: The אנשי משמר may drink wine at night but not by day. The אנשי בית אב may not drink at all, day or night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The members of the משמר may drink wine at night, but not during the day. The members of the בית אב may not drink, neither by day nor by night.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another difference between the two priestly groups, this time about drinking wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משמר is the whole week's shift, and they may only be needed during the day, so only daytime wine is forbidden. The בית אב is the family actually serving that day, and their work goes into the night too, so wine is forbidden around the clock. In Steps 4–5 the בית אב fasted less than the משמר. Both rules come from the same aim: keeping the family on duty fit for the עבודה.

phrases.english: The members of the priestly watch
are permitted to drink wine at night,
but not during the days,
and the members of the family serving that day
neither by day nor by night.
phrases.notes: The word 'may drink' is left out here, but it carries over from the line before.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר מוּתָּרִין לִשְׁתּוֹת יַיִן בַּלֵּילוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the comparison of the משמר and בית אב, moving from fasting to wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משמר: wine allowed at night only. בית אב: no wine at all.

steps.title: No haircuts or laundry during the week, except Thursday
steps.stepSummary: The אנשי משמר and אנשי מעמד may not cut hair or do laundry during their week, but on Thursday they may, out of honor for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The members of the משמר and the members of the מעמד may not cut their hair or do laundry. But on Thursday they are allowed, out of respect for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a rule that covers both the כהנים on duty and the מעמד group: no haircuts or laundry during their week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now a second group, the אנשי מעמד, is included alongside the משמר. There is one exception: Thursday is allowed so they can look clean and neat for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: the group of ordinary Jews matched to each priestly shift

phrases.english: The members of the priestly watch and the members of the non-priestly watch
are forbidden to cut hair and to launder.
But on Thursday they are permitted,
because of the honor of Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר וְאַנְשֵׁי מַעֲמָד אֲסוּרִין מִלְּסַפֵּר וּמִלְּכַבֵּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another restriction for the people on duty, and widens it to include the מעמד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No haircuts or laundry during the week of duty; Thursday is allowed for שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: This closes the משנה's rules for the people on duty: fasting depends on the stage (Steps 4–5), wine depends on the group (Step 6), and haircuts and laundry are forbidden except on Thursday (Step 7).

steps.title: Eulogies on the days around a no-eulogy holiday
steps.stepSummary: For a day listed in מגילת תענית as 'no eulogizing', the תנא קמא forbids eulogies the day before but allows them the day after. רבי יוסי forbids both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any day that מגילת תענית marks as 'not to eulogize': eulogizing the day before is forbidden, and the day after is permitted. רבי יוסי says: both the day before and the day after are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new topic: the days right next to the small holidays listed in מגילת תענית, starting with days on which eulogies are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holiday itself clearly has no eulogies. The question is how far the ban spreads. The תנא קמא spreads it one day earlier only, while רבי יוסי spreads it one day in both directions.

keyTerms.meaning: an ancient list of happy days on which fasting or eulogizing is not allowed
'not to eulogize' (the Aramaic wording in the list)

phrases.english: Any day about which it is written in Megillat Ta'anit
'not to eulogize'
the day before is forbidden; the day after is permitted.
Rabbi Yosei says:
the day before and the day after are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַכָּתוּב בִּמְגִלַּת תַּעֲנִית דְּלָא לְמִסְפַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the priestly groups and opens a new topic about מגילת תענית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: no eulogies the day before, allowed the day after. רבי יוסי: forbidden both days.

steps.title: Fasting on the days around a no-fasting holiday
steps.stepSummary: For a day listed only as 'no fasting', the תנא קמא allows fasting both the day before and the day after. רבי יוסי forbids the day before and allows the day after.
steps.simpleTranslation: A day marked 'not to fast': fasting the day before and the day after is permitted. רבי יוסי says: the day before is forbidden, and the day after is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now handles the lighter kind of holiday in the list, where only fasting is banned, and again asks about the days next to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'no fasting' day is a lower level than a 'no eulogizing' day, so everything moves one step more lenient. The תנא קמא now allows both surrounding days. רבי יוסי, who forbade both days for eulogies, now forbids only the day before.

keyTerms.meaning: 'not to fast' (the Aramaic wording in the list)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two lists. 'No eulogizing' days are stricter than 'no fasting' days, so the rules about the surrounding days are stricter for eulogies.

phrases.english: 'Not to fast'
phrases.notes: These are days where the list only says not to fast, not the stricter 'not to eulogize' days.

phrases.english: the day before and the day after are permitted.
Rabbi Yosei says:
the day before is forbidden; the day after is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel case to Step 8, for the lighter kind of holiday.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: fasting is allowed on both surrounding days. רבי יוסי: not the day before, but allowed the day after.

steps.title: Do not start a public fast series on Thursday
steps.stepSummary: A series of public fasts may not begin on a Thursday, so prices do not shoot up. The first three fasts are Monday, Thursday, Monday, and the second three are Thursday, Monday, Thursday.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not decree a public fast that starts on a Thursday, so that prices will not jump. Instead, the first three fasts are Monday, Thursday, and Monday, and the second three are Thursday, Monday, and Thursday.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה returns to the series of public fasts and teaches which weekday the series may start on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the very first fast fell on Thursday, everyone would rush to buy food on Friday for after the fast and for שבת, and sellers would raise prices. So the series must start on Monday. The תנא קמא applies this worry only to the very first fast, so the second set may start on Thursday.
steps.confusionAlert: The rule is only about the very beginning of the series. The second set of three really does start on a Thursday, and the תנא קמא allows that.

phrases.english: We do not decree a fast on the community
starting on a Thursday,
so as not to raise prices.
Rather, the first three fasts are:
Monday, Thursday, and Monday,
and the second three:
Thursday, Monday, and Thursday.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין גּוֹזְרִין תַּעֲנִית עַל הַצִּבּוּר בַּתְּחִילָּה בַּחֲמִישִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from מגילת תענית back to scheduling the public fasts for rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fast series may not begin on Thursday. Order: Mon–Thu–Mon, then Thu–Mon–Thu.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that חכמים plan public fasts with care for the community's real-life costs, not only the fasting itself.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: no set of fasts starts on Thursday
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי argues that just as the first set does not start on Thursday, the second and last sets should not start on Thursday either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: just as the first fasts do not start on a Thursday, so too the second fasts and the last fasts do not start on a Thursday.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the schedule given in Step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא worried only about the very first fast, so the second set may start on Thursday. רבי יוסי applies the price worry to every set, so each new set (second and last) must also begin on Monday.

keyTerms.meaning: the last ones (the final set of fasts)

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא forbids only the very first fast on Thursday. רבי יוסי says every set of fasts must begin on Monday.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Just as the first ones do not start on Thursday,
so too neither the second ones nor the last ones.
phrases.notes: The 'last ones' are the final set of seven fasts from Steps 4–5.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת בַּחֲמִישִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with Step 10's allowance for the second set to begin on Thursday.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No set of fasts, whether first, second, or last, may begin on a Thursday.

steps.title: No public fasts on festive days, but a started series continues
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a public fast is not decreed on ראש חודש, חנוכה, or פורים. If a series of fasts has already begun, רבן גמליאל says it is not interrupted.
steps.simpleTranslation: We don't declare a community fast on ראש חודש, חנוכה, or פורים. But if the fasts already started, we don't stop them. This is what רבן גמליאל says.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists days of celebration on which the community may not be told to start fasting. It then says what happens if a series of fasts was already running when one of these days came around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate rules here. First, you cannot begin a fast on these happy days. Second, according to רבן גמליאל, a series that has already begun does not get cut off when it reaches one of these days.

keyTerms.meaning: the first days of the month
they do not interrupt or stop

phrases.english: One may not decree a fast on the community
on New Moons, on Chanukah, or on Purim.
And if they already began, they do not interrupt,
phrases.notes: He means a series of fasts that started earlier and only now reaches one of these days.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabban Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's scheduling rules for public fasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Public fasts are not started on ראש חודש, חנוכה, or פורים. According to רבן גמליאל, a series already underway is not interrupted.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the series continues, but the fast is not completed
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר explains that רבן גמליאל agrees the fast is not completed on these days. The same is true of תשעה באב that falls on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: even though רבן גמליאל said we don't stop, he agreed that we don't finish the fast. The same goes for תשעה באב that falls on Friday.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר narrows רבן גמליאל's rule. You keep the series going, but on these days you do not fast all the way to nightfall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Not interrupting" and "completing" are two different things. The fast does start, but people eat before the day ends. תשעה באב on ערב שבת works the same way, so that no one enters שבת while still fasting.

keyTerms.meaning: they do not complete the fast until nightfall

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up "אֵין מַפְסִיקִין" (we don't cancel the fast) with "אֵין מַשְׁלִימִין" (we don't fast until nightfall). Both are true at the same time.
steps.whatToRemember: The series is not cancelled on festive days, but the fast is cut short, just as with תשעה באב on ערב שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אֵין מַפְסִיקִין,
phrases.english: Even though Rabban Gamliel said they do not interrupt,
he agreed that they do not complete the fast.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: And the same applies to the Ninth of Av that falls on Shabbat eve.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אֵין מַפְסִיקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits how far רבן גמליאל's ruling reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fasts that fall on these days are begun but not completed. The same is true of תשעה באב on ערב שבת.

steps.title: Does the ark ritual apply even to the first fasts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ritual of taking out the תיבה and asks whether this happens even on the first set of fasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: what is the order of the fasts? They take out the ark, and so on. Does this happen even on the first fasts?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting the משנה about taking the תיבה out to the street. It then asks whether that ritual applies to every series of fasts. This sets up a contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes the ritual without saying which fasts it belongs to. That leaves it sounding as if it applies to every fast, even the very first ones. The גמרא wants to check that reading.

keyTerms.meaning: the ark holding the ספר תורה

phrases.english: Gemara: What is the order of fast days?
They take out the ark, etc.
And even on the first ones?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the גמרא's discussion of the earlier part of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the תיבה ritual is done on all fasts, including the first series.

steps.title: A ברייתא saves the ark ritual for the last seven fasts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that on the first and second sets of three fasts people pray as usual. Only on the last seven is the תיבה taken out and ashes put on it and on people's heads.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first three and second three fasts, people go into shul and pray like on any regular day. On the last seven, they take the ark out to the town square and put ashes on it, on the נשיא's head, and on the אב בית דין's head, and everyone puts ashes on his own head. רבי נתן says they bring burnt ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets a ברייתא against the משנה. The ברייתא clearly limits the תיבה ritual to the final seven fasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seemed to apply the ritual to every fast, while the ברייתא gives it only to the last seven. That is a direct contradiction. רבי נתן adds a detail about which kind of ashes was used.

keyTerms.meaning: "and they contrasted it", which introduces a contradicting source
head of the court, second to the נשיא

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction: on the first and second three fasts
they enter the synagogue,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִתְפַּלְּלִין כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁמִּתְפַּלְּלִין כׇּל הַשָּׁנָה כּוּלָּהּ
phrases.english: and pray the way they pray the whole year
and on the last seven fasts

phrases.aramaic: מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הַתֵּיבָה לִרְחוֹבָהּ שֶׁל עִיר,
phrases.english: they take the ark out to the town square,
and put ashes on top of the ark,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְרֹאשׁ הַנָּשִׂיא, וּבְרֹאשׁ אַב בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: and on the head of the Nasi, and on the head of the head of the court,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד נוֹטֵל וְנוֹתֵן בְּרֹאשׁוֹ.
phrases.english: and each and every person takes ashes and puts them on his head.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: אֵפֶר מִקְלֶה הֵן מְבִיאִין!
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says: they bring burnt ashes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the question in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's unlimited description of the תיבה ritual.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives the ritual only to the last seven fasts, while the משנה seems to apply it to all fasts.

steps.title: רב פפא: the משנה also meant the last seven
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the משנה, too, was talking only about the last seven fasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: when the משנה taught this ritual, it was teaching about the last seven fasts.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא resolves the contradiction. He reads the משנה as describing only the final seven fasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real argument between the two sources. The משנה simply left out which fasts it meant, and the ברייתא fills in that detail.
steps.whatToRemember: The תיבה-and-ashes ritual belongs only to the last seven fasts, according to both the משנה and the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
When we learned our Mishnah too,
it was taught about the last seven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה applies the ritual to all fasts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה refers only to the last seven fasts.

steps.title: Why put ashes on the נשיא first if shame starts with the least?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה puts ashes on the נשיא first and only then on everyone else. It challenges this with רבי's rule: in a matter of shame, you start with the least important person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says ashes go on the head of the נשיא, and only after that teaches that everyone puts ashes on his own head. Is that right? Didn't רבי teach that with honors you start with the greatest, but with a curse you start with the smallest?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the order in the משנה and challenges it. Putting on ashes is a sign of disgrace, so by רבי's rule it should begin with the least important people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's ברייתא sets out a general rule for the order of honors and of disgrace. Ashes on the head is a form of disgrace, so starting with the נשיא seems backwards. Step 19 answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: "Is that so?", a word that opens a challenge

phrases.english: And on the head of the Nasi,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה again, which places ashes on the נשיא first.

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד נוֹתֵן בְּרֹאשׁוֹ.
phrases.english: and afterward it teaches that each and every person puts ashes on his head.
Is that so?! But it was taught:
Rabbi says:
In matters of greatness, one begins with the greatest,
and in matters of a curse, one begins with the least.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new question about the order in which the ashes are placed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's order of putting ashes on the נשיא before everyone else.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ashes are a disgrace, and רבי teaches that disgrace starts with the least important person.

steps.title: The sources for the rule: honor starts with the greatest, a curse starts with the least
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives a פסוק for each half of the rule. For honor, משה spoke to אהרן first. For a curse, the snake was cursed first, then חוה, then אדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: With honor, you start with the most important person, as it says: 'And משה said to אהרן, and to אלעזר and to איתמר.' With a curse, you start with the least important, for first the snake was cursed, then חוה was cursed, and only then אדם was cursed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from the last step. It shows where each half of the rule comes from, which makes the challenge against our משנה stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the honor case, אהרן is named before his sons, so the greatest comes first. In the curse case, the order goes snake, then חוה, then אדם, so the least important comes first. Putting ashes on heads is a sign of shame and suffering, so by this rule the leaders should go last, not first.

keyTerms.meaning: A curse, a matter of shame or punishment

phrases.english: In a matter of greatness, we begin with the greatest,
as it says: "And Moshe said to Aharon,
and to Elazar and to Itamar."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:6. אהרן, the greatest, is named before his sons.

phrases.english: And in a matter of a curse, we begin with the least,
for first the snake was cursed,
and afterward Chava was cursed,
and afterward Adam was cursed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא of רבי that was quoted in step 17 by giving its sources.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's rule that honor starts with the greatest and a curse starts with the least.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 10:6 (משה speaking to אהרן first) and the order of the curses in בראשית (snake, then חוה, then אדם).

steps.title: Going first is an honor for the leaders
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that putting ashes on the leaders first is not shame. It is an honor, because it tells them they are worthy to ask for mercy for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is an honor for them, because it is as if people are saying to them: You are important enough to ask for mercy on our behalf, for everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from רבי's rule. It says the leaders going first counts as honor, not shame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that ashes on the head is only a matter of shame, so the least important should go first. The answer changes how we see it: going first shows the leaders are the ones chosen to pray for the whole community. So it falls under the honor half of רבי's rule, and starting with the greatest is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: For everyone, for the whole community

phrases.english: This is an honor for them,
for people are saying to them:
You are important enough
to ask for mercy for us, on behalf of everyone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in steps 17–18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasts the act: it belongs to the honor category, not the shame category.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Putting ashes on the leaders first is a matter of shame, so by רבי's rule they should go last.
steps.terutzMaskana: Going first is an honor, since it shows they are worthy to pray for everyone, so starting with the greatest fits רבי's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: The leaders go first with the ashes because it is an honor: they are seen as worthy to ask for mercy for the whole community.

steps.title: Why don't the leaders put ashes on their own heads?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that every person puts ashes on his own head. Then it asks why the נשיא and אב בית דין have someone else put the ashes on them instead of doing it themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: Each and every person puts ashes on his own head. Let the נשיא and the אב בית דין also take ashes themselves and put them on their own heads. What is different about them, that someone else takes the ashes and puts them on their heads?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks a new question. It wants to know why the leaders get ashes from another person while everyone else does it himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats regular people and the leaders differently. Regular people put ashes on themselves, while for the נשיא and אב בית דין, someone else does it. The גמרא wants the reason for this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The head of the court, second to the נשיא

phrases.english: Each and every one puts on his own head.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. He means putting ashes on his head.

phrases.english: The Nasi and the Av Beit Din too,
let them take it themselves and put it on their own heads.
What is different
that another person takes it and puts it on them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה and opens a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the נשיא and אב בית דין have ashes put on them by someone else, unlike everyone else.

steps.title: Shaming yourself is not the same as being shamed by someone else
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא דמן קסרי begins to answer: a person who shames himself does not feel it the same way as being shamed by another person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא from קסרי said: A person who is shamed by himself is not like...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא דמן קסרי starts to answer the question from the last step. The sentence goes on past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that when someone else puts ashes on the leaders, they feel more humbled than if they did it to themselves. That is why another person places the ashes on them. The second half of the comparison, being shamed by others, comes at the start of the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not the same as

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba of Caesarea said:
One who is shamed by himself is not like...

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא דְּמִן קֵסָרִי: אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה מִתְבַּיֵּישׁ מֵעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Being shamed by yourself is not as strong as being shamed by others, so someone else puts the ashes on the leaders to humble them more.
